extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, small businesses, trade associations, legal counsel, and public commenters on the OSHA NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Tables and accompanying text in an OSHA Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) presenting economic-impact metrics for very small entities affected by the proposed standard, and beginning a discussion of RFA-required identification of potentially duplicative/overlapping federal rules. Includes cost and revenue metrics by NAICS industry and notes the discount rate used in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table: Economic Impacts on Very Small Entities Affected by the Proposed Standard With Costs Calculated Using a 2% Discount Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A tabulation (by NAICS industry) of economic impacts on very small entities affected by the proposed standard; table heading explicitly states costs are calculated using a 2% discount rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the context and methodological note for the following rows and columns; indicates the discount rate assumption (2%) used to annualize costs. (Original heading: "Table VIII.F.5—Economic Impacts on Very Small Entities Affected by the Proposed Standard With Costs Calculated Using a 2% Discount Rate")

rubrics_metrics.name: NAICS (industry classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry identifier used to group entities for the economic-impact table (e.g., 1111 Oilseed and Grain Farming, 3111 Animal Food Manufacturing, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary categorical axis for reporting entities, costs, revenues, and percentage impacts across sectors; enables sector-specific assessment of burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of entities (very small entities) in the NAICS industry affected, reported in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw population denominator used to compute average per-entity impacts and to assess scope of effect within each NAICS category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total annualized costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Total annualized cost associated with the proposed standard for the NAICS industry (dollar amount) as presented in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum of annualized compliance costs for the industry under the specified discount rate; used to understand aggregate burden on the industry sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average annualized cost per entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annualized cost allocated to each entity in the NAICS industry (dollar amount), shown in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-entity average used to evaluate the burden on a typical very small firm in the sector; helpful for comparison against revenue and for small-entity impact determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average revenue per entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported average revenue per entity in the NAICS industry (dollar amount) as shown in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a baseline to contextualize compliance costs; enables computation of cost burden as a share of revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs as % of revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratio of average annualized cost per entity to average revenue per entity, expressed as a percentage, shown in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key metric for assessing economic significance of the rule for very small entities; used in RFA/RegFlex determinations to identify disproportionate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount rate assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate used to annualize costs in the table (explicitly stated as 2% in the table heading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological choice that affects annualized cost figures; decision should be noted when comparing alternative analyses or discount-rate sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA requirement to identify duplicative/overlapping federal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) requires that the agency's initial regulatory flexibility analysis identify, 'to the extent practicable, . . .' federal rules which may duplicate, overlap, or conflict with the proposed rule (introduced under heading: 'F. Federal Rules Which May Duplicate, Overlap, or Conflict With the Proposed Rule').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must, where practicable, determine whether existing or pending federal regulations duplicate, overlap, or conflict with the proposed standard and disclose that analysis in the initial RFA. This is a procedural/legal requirement informing the regulatory-review scope and potential alternatives.
